+## reference · Google AI Search Guide – AEO & GEO still SEO
+
+- **AEO = Answer Engine Optimization; GEO = Generative Engine Optimization** – both are part of standard SEO, not separate frameworks.  
+- **Core SEO remains essential**: keyword research, quality content, technical health, and user experience still drive generative AI results.  
+- **No special files needed**: `llms.txt`, other machine‑readable AI files, or Markdown are unnecessary for inclusion in AI features.  
+- **No content chunking required**: Google’s retrieval‑augmented generation can parse multi‑topic pages; breaking content into small pieces is not recommended.  
+- **No AI‑specific rewriting**: Synonyms and general meaning are understood; avoid over‑optimizing for every long‑tail variation.  
+- **Inauthentic mentions are ineffective**: Spamming mentions or fake reviews does not improve AI rankings; focus on genuine, high‑quality signals.  
+- **Structured data not mandatory for AI**: Standard schema.org markup remains useful for rich results, but no special schema is required for generative AI features.  
+- **Prioritize non‑commodity content**: Create unique, in‑depth pieces that offer fresh insights rather than generic “how‑to” lists.  
+- **Follow existing SEO best practices**: Page speed, mobile friendliness, secure HTTPS, clear navigation, and accessible markup continue to influence AI rankings.  
+
+Sources: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide, https://www.searchenginejournal.com/googles-new-ai-search-guide-calls-aeo-and-geo-still-seo/575026/
